note: Six per host is the browser's HTTP/1.1 limit (Chromium: 'Default to allow up to 6 connections per host'; Firefox network.http.max-persistent-connections-per-server = 6). WebSockets have their own, larger pool (Chromium 255 per host, Firefox 200), and over HTTP/2 'a single HTTP/2 connection can contain multiple concurrently open streams', so on modern sites the cap rarely binds.
precise_version: Over HTTP/1.1, browsers open at most about six concurrent connections per host; WebSockets use a separate pool, and HTTP/2 multiplexes all requests over one connection.
reason: Severity medium -> low. The item states a real, widely taught HTTP/1.1 fact, and a learner who repeats '6 per host' is right for HTTP/1.1. The harmful conclusion (a WebSocket uses up one of the six) is in L-0324/L-0325, which are already wrong/medium with sourced notes. Grading the premise medium as well counts the same error twice; an inline clarification is enough.

note: Over-generalised. Graph databases are marketed for recommendations (Neo4j: 'The key technology in enabling real-time recommendations is the graph database'), but many large recommenders do not use one: Amazon's item-to-item collaborative filtering computes 'an updated list of related items for every product ... on a daily basis' from purchase statistics.
precise_version: Some teams drive recommendations through graph databases, but many large systems (e.g. Amazon's item-to-item collaborative filtering) compute them offline without one.
